key_insight: The paper shows that closing the optimization-time gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous training is fundamentally impossible under common similarity assumptions, and only a stronger combination of conditions can recover near-homogeneous time scaling.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this means simply assuming workers are “similar enough” may not justify faster asynchronous optimization guarantees; algorithm design must account for stronger structural conditions or accept heterogeneous-case slowdowns.
method: Proves impossibility results under widely used first- and second-order similarity assumptions for randomized algorithms.
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone still cannot bridge the gap.
Introduces strong interpolation plus the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition to obtain improved time complexity matching the best homogeneous dependence on worker computation times.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates the evidence is theoretical rather than experimental, centered on complexity bounds and impossibility/proof-based guarantees.
watch_item: The improved bound relies on stronger assumptions than simple data similarity, so practical applicability may be limited if real workloads do not satisfy strong interpolation and local PL conditions.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
